control_blender_ui.name: control_blender_ui
control_blender_ui.title: Control Blender Ui
control_blender_ui.description: Perform a named agent_control action in the explicitly attached Blender window. Use inspect for editor IDs, active tool, Properties tabs, shared workspace and agent cursors. Actions display labelled agent pointers; move_cursor moves this overlay, never the OS cursor. Use observe after an external screenshot to show a brief eye badge and viewport pulse. Before set_tool on a shared workspace, use isolate_workspace then inspect for new editor IDs. Uses Blender UI APIs, not physical key/click events or arbitrary button lookup. Requires attached mode; does not launch Blender or execute arbitrary scripts.

agent_control.description: inspect, observe, move_cursor, clear_cursor, open_menu, select_object, set_tool, show_properties, set_property or isolate_workspace.

target.description: Menu add/object/view, tool select_box/move/rotate/scale, object name, Properties tab such as OBJECT, or active-object property location/rotation_euler/scale.

area_id.description: Editor ID from inspect; required for editor actions with multiple matches. Object selection/property writes do not require it. Re-inspect after workspace isolation.

position.description: move_cursor only: agent overlay coordinates [x, y] in [0, 1], bottom-left origin; default center.

value.description: set_property only: three finite values for the active object; rotations in radians.

agent_id.description: Visible agent label, 1 to 64 printable characters; defaults to the MCP session identity. Use distinct stable labels for named agents across connections. clear_cursor removes only this agent's marker in the attached window; markers expire after 120 seconds.

attach_blender_window.name: attach_blender_window
attach_blender_window.title: Attach Blender Window
attach_blender_window.description: Attached mode: select the Blender process and window that Blender tools act on, the same as `simul blender attach`. Use it to recover after another file was loaded (read_homefile, open_mainfile) or Blender restarted. Succeeds only when the choice is unambiguous; pass instance_id/window_id from the error details or get_blender_info otherwise.

instance_id.description: Bridge instance ID; required when several Blender processes run.

window_id.description: Window ID; required when the selected process has several windows.

bounds_max.description: Maximum corner of the box as [x, y, z] in scene units.

capture_blender_viewport.name: capture_blender_viewport
capture_blender_viewport.title: Capture Blender Viewport
capture_blender_viewport.description: Capture Blender as a JPEG. In attached mode the default (method='auto') is the 3D View the user sees: view angle, shading, overlays, Edit Mode and unsaved edits, with no camera needed, keeping the view's aspect ratio within width x height (capture_method viewport; an external engine's Rendered view, such as Cycles, is read from the screen as viewport_screen and includes overlapping UI). Embedded (headless bpy) mode has no 3D View, so 'auto' renders. method='render' renders through the scene camera, or through a temporary camera removed afterwards: aligned to the 3D View when attached, framing the visible objects when embedded or when the window shows no 3D View (render_temp_camera_view / render_temp_camera_framing). The image arrives as an MCP image content block, followed by a JSON block with success, width, height, engine, capture_method, format and image_attached=true. In attached mode, briefly show an agent eye badge and border pulse after success. Agent annotations are excluded from the captured image.

width.description: Maximum image width in pixels. A viewport capture, or a render through a temporary camera aligned to the 3D View, keeps the view's aspect ratio inside width x height; other renders are exactly width x height.

height.description: Maximum image height in pixels; see width.

method.description: "viewport": the 3D View as the user sees it (view angle, shading, overlays, Edit Mode, unsaved changes); attached mode only. "render": a render through the scene camera, or through a temporary camera when the scene has none (aligned to the 3D View when attached, framing the visible objects otherwise), removed afterwards. "auto" (default): "viewport" when attached, "render" in embedded mode.

agent_id.description: Visible capture feedback label in attached mode; ignored in embedded mode.

set_blender_camera_view.name: set_blender_camera_view
set_blender_camera_view.title: Set Blender Camera View
set_blender_camera_view.description: Place a Blender camera (the active one by default) at a world-space location and XYZ Euler rotation, whatever its parent and rotation mode. Success means the placement is in the camera's transform; its constraints (Track To, Copy Location, Child Of, ...) still apply and are never muted. location and rotation_euler report where Blender evaluates the camera; placement_overridden is true when that is not the request, with constraints_applied and a warning on how to disable them. Keys on the camera's transform take over at the next frame change. Blender's viewport skips a camera disabled in viewports unless it is needed by something visible, or is the scene camera or a timeline marker's camera and its hide_viewport is not animated: when Blender did not evaluate it after the placement (or its evaluated pose did not change), override_check is 'skipped' and placement_overridden null.

rotation_euler.description: World-space camera rotation [rx, ry, rz] in radians, as an XYZ Euler.

camera_name.description: Target camera name. Uses active camera when None.

get_blender_camera_info.name: get_blender_camera_info
get_blender_camera_info.title: Get Blender Camera Info
get_blender_camera_info.description: Get a Blender camera's world-space location and XYZ Euler rotation where Blender evaluates it (constraints included), the constraints that act on it (constraints_applied), lens and clip range (the active camera by default). Blender keeps a stale pose for a camera disabled in viewports unless it is needed by something visible through a child, a constraint or a modifier, or is the scene camera or a timeline marker's camera and its hide_viewport is not animated: its pose is then composed from its own transform (pose_source 'transform'), without its constraints, drivers and keys, and warning says what that leaves out.

camera_name.description: Target camera name. Uses active camera when None.

focus_blender_on_object.name: focus_blender_on_object
focus_blender_on_object.title: Focus Blender On Object
focus_blender_on_object.description: Frame a Blender object with a camera (the active one by default): aim it from the front and above at the object's bounding-box center, at the distance where the object fits the frame (an orthographic camera gets the ortho_scale that fits it), widening the clip range when it would cut the object away. As with set_blender_camera_view, success means the framing is in the camera's transform and its constraints still apply: camera_location and camera_rotation_euler report where Blender evaluates the camera, and placement_overridden is true when constraints or drivers moved it off the framing. For a camera disabled in viewports that Blender did not evaluate after the placement (or whose evaluated pose did not change), override_check is 'skipped' and placement_overridden null.

distance_factor.description: Multiple of the framing distance (of ortho_scale for an orthographic camera): 1.0 fits the object's bounding sphere in the frame with 5% to spare, 2.0 shows the object at half that size, and below 1.0 crops it.

camera_name.description: Target camera name. Uses active camera when None.

get_blender_viewport_info.name: get_blender_viewport_info
get_blender_viewport_info.title: Get Blender Viewport Info
get_blender_viewport_info.description: Get active viewport and render settings.

capture_blender_viewport_sequence.name: capture_blender_viewport_sequence
capture_blender_viewport_sequence.title: Capture Blender Viewport Sequence
capture_blender_viewport_sequence.description: Capture a frame range as base64-encoded JPEGs, each made like capture_blender_viewport with the same method (the 3D View when attached, a camera render in embedded mode). In attached mode, briefly show an agent eye badge and border pulse after success. Agent annotations are excluded from the captured images.

width.description: Maximum image width, as for capture_blender_viewport.

height.description: Maximum image height, as for capture_blender_viewport.

agent_id.description: Visible capture feedback label in attached mode; ignored in embedded mode.

create_blender_object.title: Create Blender Object

rotation_euler.description: New rotation [rx, ry, rz] or None to keep current.

clear_blender_object_parent.description: Remove parent from a Blender object.

assign_blender_material.name: assign_blender_material
assign_blender_material.title: Assign Blender Material
assign_blender_material.description: Assign a Principled BSDF material to a Blender object. A material of that name is reused (repeating the call changes nothing more; reuse_existing=false creates a new one), and shading arguments left out keep the material's values, so an existing material can be assigned as it is. By default it replaces the object's material: slot 0, every face. slot_index puts it in one slot (the slot count adds one); face_indices assigns it to those faces only. link='OBJECT' keeps it off linked duplicates sharing the mesh. base_color is RGB or RGBA in 0-1; alpha below 1 sets the Principled Alpha and blended rendering (exported as USD opacity). Image textures can drive base color, metallic, roughness and normal (they need a UV map: uv_unwrap_blender_mesh). Blender's USD exporter writes UsdPreviewSurface; it does not write OmniPBR or MDL. Everything is checked first; a failure leaves nothing behind.

object_name.description: Object to assign the material to (mesh, curve, text, or another type with material slots).

base_color.description: RGB or RGBA in [0, 1]; the alpha becomes the Principled Alpha, and below 1 the material renders blended.

slot_index.description: Slot to put the material in; the slot count adds one.

face_indices.description: Mesh faces to assign the material to.

link.description: DATA (the mesh's slot) or OBJECT (this object's slot).

reuse_existing.description: Reuse a material of that name when one exists.

normal_texture.description: Tangent-space normal map image (Non-Color), through a Normal Map node.

add_blender_modifier.name: add_blender_modifier
add_blender_modifier.title: Add Blender Modifier
add_blender_modifier.description: Add a modifier to a Blender mesh, curve or other object with a modifier stack. params are the modifier's settings by Blender RNA name, checked before use: an unknown name is refused with the closest names, an enum value must be one of its items, a number must lie within the setting's limits (Blender would clamp it silently), and an object or collection setting takes its name, e.g. {'object': 'Cutter'} for BOOLEAN. The reply echoes the stored settings. A refused call leaves no modifier behind. DECIMATE is refused on a mesh with invalid geometry, which can freeze Blender; run clean_blender_mesh first.

params.description: Modifier settings by RNA name, e.g. {"ratio": 0.5} for DECIMATE or {"object": "Cutter"} for BOOLEAN.

apply_blender_modifier.name: apply_blender_modifier
apply_blender_modifier.title: Apply Blender Modifier
apply_blender_modifier.description: Apply one modifier of a Blender mesh object, baking its result into the mesh data (for example a Decimate before export) and removing it from the stack. A modifier below others is applied to the base mesh without them, with a warning; shared mesh data is copied for this object first. A modifier disabled in the viewport is refused, as Blender would drop it unapplied. Requires Object Mode.

modifier_name.description: Name of the modifier to apply.

remove_blender_modifier.name: remove_blender_modifier
remove_blender_modifier.title: Remove Blender Modifier
remove_blender_modifier.description: Remove one modifier from a Blender object's stack without applying it.

modifier_name.description: Name of the modifier to remove.

set_blender_light_params.name: set_blender_light_params
set_blender_light_params.title: Set Blender Light Params
set_blender_light_params.description: Set a Blender light's parameters, optionally changing its type first (light_type). Each setting must belong to the light's type: shadow_soft_size is the radius of POINT and SPOT lights, spot_size and spot_blend are SPOT's, angle is a SUN's softness, and shape, size and size_y are an AREA light's; others are refused, as are values outside Blender's limits (which it would clamp silently) and negative energy. The reply echoes every setting of the light's type as stored.

energy.description: Light power in watts (irradiance in W/m² for SUN), >= 0.

color.description: Light color RGB [r, g, b], each >= 0.

spot_size.description: Spot cone angle in radians, 1 degree to pi (SPOT).

shadow_soft_size.description: Light radius for soft shadows, >= 0 (POINT, SPOT).

light_type.description: Change the light to POINT, SUN, SPOT or AREA first.

angle.description: Sun's angular diameter in radians, 0 to pi (SUN).

size.description: Area light size, >= 0 (AREA; its width for RECTANGLE and ELLIPSE).

size_y.description: Area light height, >= 0 (AREA with shape RECTANGLE or ELLIPSE).

shape.description: Area light shape: SQUARE, RECTANGLE, DISK or ELLIPSE (AREA).

open_blender_file.name: open_blender_file
open_blender_file.title: Open Blender File
open_blender_file.description: Open a .blend file, replacing the current scene. Refuses with UnsavedChangesError while the open file has unsaved changes (in attached mode every agent edit counts, as each is an undo step); save them first with save_blender_file, or pass discard_unsaved=true to discard them.

discard_unsaved.description: Open even though the current file has unsaved changes, which are then lost. To keep them, save first with save_blender_file.

file_path.description: Path to save to. None saves in place.

import_blender_file.name: import_blender_file
import_blender_file.title: Import Blender File
import_blender_file.description: Import a file into the Blender scene.

export_blender_file.title: Export Blender File
export_blender_file.description: Export scene objects to a file.

file_format.description: One of OBJ, FBX, GLTF, USD, STL, PLY.

selected_only.description: If True, export only selected objects.

get_blender_file_info.title: Get Blender File Info
get_blender_file_info.description: Get information about the current .blend file.

get_blender_frame.title: Get Blender Frame
get_blender_frame.description: Get the current frame and animation range.

insert_blender_keyframe.title: Insert Blender Keyframe

get_blender_keyframes.title: Get Blender Keyframes

setup_blender_rigid_body.title: Setup Blender Rigid Body
setup_blender_rigid_body.description: Set up rigid body physics on a Blender object.

add_blender_force_field.title: Add Blender Force Field
add_blender_force_field.description: Add a force field to the scene.

get_blender_force_field_info.title: Get Blender Force Field Info

add_blender_rigid_body_constraint.title: Add Blender Rigid Body Constraint
add_blender_rigid_body_constraint.description: Add a rigid body constraint between two objects.

location.description: Optional world-space location for the constraint empty.

get_blender_constraint_info.title: Get Blender Constraint Info
get_blender_constraint_info.description: Get rigid body constraint info for an object.

get_blender_physics_state.title: Get Blender Physics State
get_blender_physics_state.description: Get current physics state of an object.

get_blender_object_trajectory.title: Get Blender Object Trajectory
get_blender_object_trajectory.description: Sample object position over a frame range.

bake_blender_simulation.name: bake_blender_simulation
bake_blender_simulation.title: Bake Blender Simulation
bake_blender_simulation.description: Bake physics simulation for a frame range.

execute_blender_script.name: execute_blender_script
execute_blender_script.title: Execute Blender Script
execute_blender_script.description: Execute arbitrary Python code inside Blender with access to bpy. Assign to __result__ to return a value. Printed output comes back in output, cut to its first max_output_chars characters (default 32000, at most 100000), or earlier when they exceed 300000 bytes of JSON (heavily non-ASCII output); a cut sets output_truncated=true and output_total_chars to the full length. Write larger results to a file and return its path instead. Anything the script raises, including SystemExit from sys.exit(), is reported in error and never ends Blender. In attached mode each call is one undo step.

timeout.description: Maximum wall-clock seconds to wait for the script; ``None`` waits for it to finish.

max_output_chars.description: Most characters of printed output to return, 1 to 100000 (default 32000). Longer output is cut to its first max_output_chars characters with output_truncated=true and output_total_chars set. Output that JSON escapes heavily (non-ASCII text, control characters) is cut earlier, at 300000 bytes of JSON, so the prefix always arrives. Write larger results to a file and return its path instead.

create_blender_mesh_from_data.name: create_blender_mesh_from_data
create_blender_mesh_from_data.title: Create Blender Mesh From Data
create_blender_mesh_from_data.description: Create a mesh object from raw vertex, edge, and face data. Use for procedural geometry. Each vertex is exactly [x, y, z] finite numbers; a face repeating a vertex or another face's vertex set, an edge joining a vertex to itself or repeating another, and a collection outside the current scene are refused before anything is created. The mesh is validated, and a failed call leaves no mesh or object behind.

vertices.description: Vertex positions, each exactly [x, y, z] finite numbers.

edges.description: Loose edges as [v0, v1] pairs of two different vertices; face edges are made from the faces.

faces.description: Faces as lists of three or more vertex indices, each vertex once and each vertex set once.

collection_name.description: Target collection in the current scene (the scene collection if None).

clean_blender_mesh.name: clean_blender_mesh
clean_blender_mesh.title: Clean Blender Mesh
clean_blender_mesh.description: Repair a Blender mesh object's data. Always validates it, removing faces that repeat a vertex and duplicate faces or edges (geometry that can freeze Decimate); then optionally merges vertices within merge_distance, dissolves edges and faces smaller than dissolve_degenerate_distance, and recalculates normals to point outside. Reports the counts before and after. Shared mesh data changes for every object using it. Requires Object Mode.

object_name.description: Mesh object whose data to clean.

merge_distance.description: Merge vertices within this distance; None skips it.

dissolve_degenerate_distance.description: Dissolve edges and faces smaller than this; None skips it.

recalculate_normals.description: Make face normals point consistently outside.

uv_unwrap_blender_mesh.name: uv_unwrap_blender_mesh
uv_unwrap_blender_mesh.title: Uv Unwrap Blender Mesh
uv_unwrap_blender_mesh.description: Generate UV coordinates for every face of a Blender mesh object, as image textures need: SMART_PROJECT (Smart UV Project: islands split at angle_limit, packed with island_margin) or CUBE_PROJECT (each face projected onto the cube side it faces). Writes uv_map_name (created when missing), else the active UV map, else a new UVMap. Enters Edit Mode briefly and restores the selection and active object. Requires Object Mode.

uv_map_name.description: UV map to write; the active one (or a new UVMap) if omitted.

angle_limit.description: SMART_PROJECT: island angle in radians, above 0 to pi/2.

cube_size.description: CUBE_PROJECT: size of the projection cube, above 0.

apply_simready_metadata.title: Apply Simready Metadata
apply_simready_metadata.description: Apply NVIDIA SimReady metadata (semantic labels, physics properties, material info) to a Blender object as custom properties. Stored with simready_ prefix for USD export.

metadata.description: Dict with optional keys ``semantic``, ``physics``, ``material``, each containing relevant sub-fields.

get_simready_metadata.name: get_simready_metadata
get_simready_metadata.title: Get Simready Metadata
get_simready_metadata.description: Read NVIDIA SimReady metadata from a Blender object. Returns semantic labels, physics properties, and material info stored as simready_ custom properties.

validate_simready_compliance.name: validate_simready_compliance
validate_simready_compliance.title: Validate Simready Compliance
validate_simready_compliance.description: Validate Blender objects against NVIDIA SimReady conventions: naming (lowercase_underscore), scale (meters), clean transforms, material segmentation, hierarchy.

object_names.description: Objects to check.  ``None`` checks all mesh objects.

export_simready_usd.name: export_simready_usd
export_simready_usd.title: Export Simready Usd
export_simready_usd.description: Export a SimReady-compliant USD file from Blender. Validates objects before export, selects the requested objects, and carries simready_ custom properties into USD attributes.

setup_simready_hierarchy.name: setup_simready_hierarchy
setup_simready_hierarchy.title: Setup Simready Hierarchy
setup_simready_hierarchy.description: Create a SimReady-compliant object hierarchy in Blender with a root empty (XForm equivalent) and parent the given children under it. Optionally applies semantic labels to the root.

root_name.description: Name for the root empty object.

child_names.description: Existing objects to parent under the root.

semantic.description: Optional semantic labels dict to apply to the root.
